risks.note: The Company changed its principal business from Information Technology and software services to the trading of pharmaceutical, hygiene and cleanroom products during FY2025-26 and states it 'is presently in the initial stage of business transformation' and 'in the initial phase of developing its pharmaceutical trading business'. Its FY2025-26 revenue from operations still came from the legacy technology business (Projects & Services and Software Sales), so sourcing arrangements, the distribution network and the customer base all remain to be built. Management's outlook rests on industry fundamentals rather than an established book of business.
risks.risk: Unproven business transformation - the pharmaceutical trading business is still at inception with essentially no revenue behind it

risks.note: Management states that wholesale distributors must comply with regulations on drug licensing, storage conditions, product traceability, GST compliance and quality standards under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and related regulations, and that any change in regulatory requirements may increase compliance costs and impact operations. Changes in healthcare regulations and product quality risk are also listed among the business risks.
risks.risk: Regulatory compliance risk in one of India's most regulated sectors

risks.note: The MD&A flags increasing pressure on product pricing from government regulation under the Drug Price Control Order (DPCO), competition among distributors and procurement by institutional buyers, and states that 'sustaining profitability while maintaining competitive pricing remains a key challenge'. For a pure trading model with no manufacturing value-add, margin is the whole economics.
risks.risk: Pricing pressure and thin trading margins

risks.note: The distribution business depends on timely procurement and uninterrupted supply from manufacturers; the Company flags that disruption from raw material shortages, transportation bottlenecks, geopolitical developments or manufacturing delays may impact product availability and customer service. The Company has no manufacturing of its own and is still establishing supplier relationships.
risks.risk: Supply chain and sourcing dependency on third-party manufacturers

risks.note: Management states the wholesale pharmaceutical business generally requires adequate working capital to hold inventory and extend credit to customers, and separately recognises risks relating to customer credit, liquidity management and operational continuity. Shareholders' funds fell to Rs.17.88 Lakhs as on 31st March 2026 from Rs.63.95 Lakhs a year earlier because of the year's loss, and the Company reports no debt raised, so the balance sheet supporting any inventory-and-receivables build is thin.
risks.risk: Working capital intensity and customer credit / liquidity risk against a very small equity base

risks.note: The Indian pharmaceutical distribution market is described as comprising several organised and unorganised players competing on pricing, product availability and customer service; the Company is a new entrant with no established distribution footprint, and management says continuous improvement in operational efficiency, customer relationships and product portfolio will be essential to remain competitive.
risks.risk: Intense competition from organised and unorganised distributors

risks.note: The MD&A attributes the FY2025-26 loss to higher employee benefit expenses, administrative costs and 'penalties incurred during the year', and the note to the key-ratio table states explicitly that the change in profitability and margin ratios is 'mainly due to the reason that the profit / (loss) for the current year is impacted due to penalty charged by BSE Limited and increased employee benefit expenses'. This is a disclosed compliance failure with a real earnings consequence, not process boilerplate.
risks.risk: Listing-compliance lapse - a penalty charged by BSE Limited materially affected the year's result

risks.note: June Enterprises Private Limited acquired 60.88% of the share capital under the promoter category via a Share Purchase Agreement dated 05 March 2025 and a SEBI (SAST) open offer, making the Company its subsidiary. Across FY2025-26 the entire executive and much of the non-executive bench changed: the Managing Director, a Director who was also Chief Financial Officer, and another Director resigned effective 24th May 2025, two more directors resigned w.e.f. 14th August 2025, a new MD and Whole-Time Director were appointed w.e.f. 23rd May 2025, three Independent Directors w.e.f. 21st July 2025, and both the CFO and the Company Secretary & Compliance Officer positions changed hands during the year. Sixteen board meetings were required. Execution of the new strategy depends entirely on an untested management team.
risks.risk: Change of control and near-complete turnover of the board and key managerial personnel
